seoTitle: How to Issue a Partial Refund to an eBay Buyer as a Seller
metaDescription: See how to issue a partial refund on eBay from Seller Hub, adjust the amount manually, and keep the order intact instead of cancelling the sale.
intro: When a buyer receives a slightly damaged item or agrees to keep a product for a reduced price, cancelling the whole order is overkill — a partial refund settles the issue while keeping the transaction on record. This guide walks through where to find that option in eBay, starting from signing in through to locating the order in Seller Hub, so you can resolve the complaint without a return shipment or a dispute. It applies across most eBay categories, from electronics to clothing to collectibles.

steps.heading: Sign in to your eBay account
steps.body: Start at eBay's sign-in screen and enter your email or username, or use one of the Google, Facebook, or Apple continue options if your account is linked to one of them. Leaving "Stay signed in" checked saves you from re-authenticating every time you check on an order, which matters if you're processing refunds regularly as part of running a store. Once you're in, everything for managing an order — refunds included — is reachable from your account menu rather than the public storefront pages.

steps.heading: Head to My eBay and find your selling tools
steps.body: After signing in, go to My eBay from the top navigation, which opens to an Activity summary with links down the left side for Purchases, Watchlist, and — for sellers — a Selling section. This page itself doesn't process refunds, but it's the hub that gets you to Seller Hub or the Orders view where the actual order lives. If you sell regularly, bookmarking Seller Hub directly saves a click over going through this summary every time.

image.caption: The My eBay Activity summary. Selling tools sit in the left-hand menu, one level away from the order you need.

steps.heading: Locate the order in Seller Hub
steps.body: In Seller Hub's orders list, each row shows the item, buyer, tracking number, price, and order status like Shipped or Delivered. Find the specific order the buyer contacted you about — searching by buyer name or order number is faster than scrolling once you have more than a handful of orders — and open it. This is also where you'd confirm the item actually shipped and what tracking shows, useful context before you decide how much to refund.

image.caption: Seller Hub's order list, showing item details, tracking numbers, and order status for each sale.

steps.heading: Choose refund instead of cancelling the order
steps.body: On the order's detail view, look for the refund action rather than any cancel option — cancelling unwinds the whole sale, while refund keeps the order and its history intact and just adjusts how much money changed hands. This distinction matters for your records and for the buyer's experience: a refund reads as you standing behind the sale, while a cancellation can look like the transaction never happened, which is confusing when the buyer already has the item.

steps.heading: Enter the partial amount and a reason
steps.body: Instead of accepting the full order total, type in the specific amount you've agreed to refund — say, a portion of the price to compensate for minor damage. eBay will typically ask for a reason for the refund, which is worth filling in accurately since it becomes part of the order's record if the buyer or eBay support ever needs to review the case later.

steps.heading: Confirm with the buyer and follow up if needed
steps.body: Submit the refund, then message the buyer to let them know it's been issued and why — this small step does a lot to prevent a dispute from escalating, since the buyer isn't left guessing whether the seller actually acted. If the buyer doesn't accept the offer or continues to push for more, eBay's resolution center is the next stop rather than negotiating back and forth indefinitely in messages. A partial refund handled promptly and communicated clearly is one of the more reliable ways to protect your feedback score after a minor issue.

faq.question: Does a partial refund on eBay affect my seller metrics?
faq.answer: Refunds, including partial ones, can factor into your seller performance data, though a smoothly handled partial refund is generally better for metrics than a full cancellation or a dispute.

faq.question: Can a buyer reject a partial refund offer?
faq.answer: Yes, the buyer can decline the offer, in which case you may need to negotiate further or escalate through eBay's resolution center.

faq.question: How long does a partial refund take to reach the buyer?
faq.answer: Processing times follow eBay's standard refund timelines, which usually means the funds appear back on the buyer's payment method within a few business days.

faq.question: Do I need to accept a return to issue a partial refund?
faq.answer: No, a partial refund can be issued without requiring the buyer to return the item, which is one of the main reasons sellers use it for minor issues.
